A winning start to the sporting year! On Wednesday the u14 girls played their first game of the year against Townley Grammar School. We won! 2-0! The girls played great and they are looking forward to playing the many upcoming games this season! Miss Forbes, PE Teacher #commitment #Pride #success
𝐅𝐞𝐞𝐥-𝐆𝐨𝐨𝐝 𝐅𝐫𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝐚𝐭 𝐂𝐥𝐞𝐞𝐯𝐞 𝐏𝐚𝐫𝐤 Friday is Feel-Good Friday at Cleeve Park School! This week, teachers were asked to nominate five students who have demonstrated our school values of Commitment, Pride and Success during their first few days with us. Our lucky five were Carter, Arjun, Daisy, Louis and Betsy, who were rewarded with a delicious hot chocolate. While enjoying their treat, we had a lovely and productive conversation about how they have found their first few days at Cleeve Park. The students shared lots of positive feedback. They told us that the food is nice, the teachers and other students are kind and helpful, and the Sixth Formers have made them feel welcome. They also praised our excellent facilities, the huge field, the canopy and the wide range of equipment available to help them feel comfortable. Most importantly, they said they are really enjoying their lessons. One student summed it up perfectly by saying, “𝑨𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒚, 𝒆𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚𝒕𝒉𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒊𝒔 𝒋𝒖𝒔𝒕 𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒇𝒆𝒄𝒕!” Well done to our first five Feel-Good Friday winners! Mr Moloney Head of Behaviour, Inclusion and Transition

Thankfully the sun decided to put his hat on (and the rain stayed away) during our busiest times. During the last week we had the new year 7 Induction Day, multiple offsite trips & visits, KS3 Prize Giving, Year 10 Work Experience and Aspiration Day, Year 7 PGL and of course, the fantastic Resilience Day. pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
Our Vision is:
To provide an excellent education for all our students.
Our Values are:
Commitment, Pride, Success
Commitment to learning; Pride in ourselves and our community; Success in all we do.
To create a place of learning where excellence is sought in every sphere
To provide a stimulating environment and lessons which show pupils that learning is exciting and worthwhile as a life-long activity
To encourage methods of learning which depend upon pupil activity and the development of learning and research skills
To provide courses which are appropriate to life in contemporary society
To prepare pupils for responsible adulthood – in the family, in the workplace and in the community
To help pupils develop a wide range of interests
To help pupils recognise the value of honesty, courtesy, helpfulness and self-discipline
To help pupils value the spiritual and aesthetic dimensions of life

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Cleeve Park School is a thriving 11-18 community with a clear vision: to provide an excellent education for all.
We are guided by our values of commitment, pride, and success. We foster a commitment to learning, encouraging every student to embrace opportunities with determination and resilience. We nurture pride in ourselves and our community, celebrating the unique contributions of every individual and cultivating a sense of belonging. Ultimately, we aim for success in all we do, inspiring students to achieve and exceed their aspirations.
Our students are our greatest asset. We are proud to see them grow into confident, articulate, and thoughtful young people, continually impressing us with their talents and ambitions. Our inclusive ethos ensures that every student is valued, supported, and challenged to reach their full potential.
We have a dedicated and highly skilled staff team, committed to delivering a curriculum that is inspiring, stimulating, and thought-provoking. Together with parents and carers, we cultivate positive attitudes, resilience, and a shared belief in achieving beyond expectations.
Our facilities reflect our commitment to excellence, including a 3G pitch, state-of-the-art performing arts block, industry-standard fitness centre, newly refurbished science laboratories, and enhanced design and technology spaces. These resources provide an excellent environment for learning, growth, and creativity.
We invite you to explore our website, learn more about our school and discover why Cleeve Park School is the ideal place for your child to thrive.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Post Sixteen at Cleeve Park School
At Cleeve Park, we offer a Post 16 education that prepares students for whatever their next step in life holds. Not all students know what they want to do when they finish school, so we see it as our responsibility and honour to support young people navigate this stage of their education, preparing them for the known and unknown world ahead.
For September 2026 we will be offering the following pathways:
Throughout Years 12 and 13 to each member of our sixth form will be given the expert advice and guidance required to assist with the next step in their lives Post 18, be it university, apprenticeship or employment.
We provide a comprehensive curriculum that will enable young people to specialise or have a broad Key Stage 5 offer that will allow choices to be made at a later stage. We have excellent facilities that support the independent learning that is required at Key Stage 5, but also maintain the pastoral and social support that young people need.
Students in our sixth form are provided with a Chromebook to work on in school and at home and access to the school WIFI.
Our pastoral team ensure that our Post 16 students are encouraged to build skills of resilience and independence but also we understand that this is not necessarily straightforward or easy.
Students have access to a private study suite fully equipped with computers staffed by an experienced Study Supervisor. We have also introduced silent study rooms, timetabled for every period, to provide an environment for extended writing and literary learning for those students whose needs require a smaller environment.
Sixth Form students also have their own canteen which provides a more relaxed environment at break and lunch away from the main part of the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: RSE Information - TKAT Cleeve Park School
pageCache.text:
RSE Information
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHE) is our comprehensive curriculum for supporting young people's personal development, health, wellbeing and understanding of relationships. We use the Jigsaw national curriculum to help us achieve this.
We are required by law to teach Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education to all secondary-aged pupils. We deliver these statutory subjects within our broader PSHE programme, which also includes elements of age-appropriate economic education (preparing young people to understand financial matters and the world of work) and citizenship education (including fundamental British values, helping pupils understand their rights, responsibilities and role in society).
The DfE statutory guidance (July 2025) states:
"Children and young people need knowledge and skills that will enable them to make informed and ethical decisions about their wellbeing, health and relationships. High quality, evidence-based teaching of relationships, sex and health education (RSHE) can help prepare pupils for the opportunities and responsibilities of adult life, and can promote their moral, social, mental and physical development."
The Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) policy explains our whole-school approach to RSE/PSHE education and how we meet our statutory duties, a copy can be found here.
To withdraw your child from the Sex Education component of RSE please complete this form.

pageCache.pageTitle: Jumpers for Jimmy - 12th December 2025 - News - TKAT Cleeve Park School
pageCache.text:
Jumpers for Jimmy - 12th December 2025
We are inviting all students and staff to participate in our annual Christmas jumper day, this year proudly named ‘Jumpers for Jimmy’, taking place on Friday, 12th December.
This event is dedicated to raising vital funds for the Mizen Foundation, an organisation established in memory of Jimmy Mizen. Jimmy was tragically murdered in the local area in 2008. Since then, his parents, Barry and Margaret, have worked tirelessly to ensure Jimmy's legacy lives on by promoting the powerful message of Forgiveness, Hope, and Peace throughout schools and communities, more details can be found on their website http://www.jimmymizen.org.uk/
Supporting the Sparkle Award
Our fundraising efforts this year will specifically support the Foundation’s Sparkle Award. This award is designed to shine a spotlight on the extraordinary acts of kindness, support, and positive community impact demonstrated by young individuals.
The Sparkle Award celebrates those young people who may not always receive academic accolades but whose character and actions make an indelible impact on the atmosphere and well-being of their schools and local communities. It is a true celebration of community spirit and positive values.
On Friday, 12th December, we encourage all students and staff to wear a festive jumper over their school shirt and tie along with their usual uniform. In return for wearing their jumper, we are asking for a small voluntary donation, which will go directly to funding the Mizen Foundation’s Sparkle Award. Please use our Just Giving Page here to make a donation:
https://www.justgiving.com/page/cleeveparkxmasjumperday
We believe that supporting the Mizen Foundation directly reinforces the values of kindness, community and respect that we promote every day in our school.
Thank you in advance for your generosity and participation. We look forward to a day of festive spirit and meaningful giving.
Mr Stone, Assistant Headteacher
